subject: Cloud Computing
title: Cloud vs. On-Premises Economics
description: A quick, practical guide to Cloud vs. On-Premises Economics.

hook.text: Dropbox spent $75 million on cloud. Then it built its own data centers and saved half. Was cloud a mistake?

buildup.text: At massive scale, owning hardware can beat cloud pricing. The breakeven point depends on utilization and growth.

discovery.text: Cloud wins for variable workloads. On-premises wins for steady, predictable, high-volume usage.

twist.text: Most companies aren't Dropbox-scale. For them, the operational burden of on-premises outweighs the savings.

climax.text: The answer isn't cloud or on-premises. Many companies use both — a hybrid approach that optimizes for cost.

punchline.text: Cloud or own? It depends on scale, skills, and workload.

quiz.question: When does owning hardware typically beat cloud pricing?
options: At very large scale with steady, predictable workloads
Always, since hardware is cheaper per hour than cloud
Only for companies with fewer than 10 employees

details.summary: On-premises requires buying, housing, and maintaining hardware upfront. Cloud shifts these to operating expenses paid monthly. Cloud costs more per unit at scale but offers elasticity, faster deployment, and no maintenance burden. The total cost comparison depends on workload patterns.
details.whyItMatters: The cloud vs on-prem decision affects company finances for years. Oversimplified comparisons ignore operational costs, opportunity costs, and the value of speed that cloud provides.
takeaways: On-prem has high upfront CapEx; cloud is ongoing OpEx
Cloud costs more per unit but includes operations and elasticity
Total cost depends on utilization, team size, and growth rate

faq.question: When is on-premises cheaper than cloud?
faq.answer: On-premises can be cheaper for large, predictable, steady-state workloads with high utilization where the organization has skilled operations staff. Companies like Dropbox and Basecamp have saved money moving some workloads off cloud at scale.

faq.question: What hidden costs does on-premises have?
faq.answer: Hidden costs include facilities, power, cooling, physical security, hardware refresh cycles, operational staff salaries, spare parts inventory, software licensing, and the opportunity cost of slow provisioning. These often double the hardware-only cost estimate.
